name: Edgehold
shortDescription: Make the pointer cross between displays on purpose instead of by accident.
longDescription: On a multi-display desk the pointer slips onto the wrong screen constantly. Edgehold adds configurable behaviour at each boundary between displays — resistance, a deliberate second push, a modifier key, or a single crossing point — while leaving pointer movement everywhere else completely normal. Once it is configured you should stop noticing it.
statusNote: In planning. Details will be published as development progresses.
highlights: Rules configured per boundary, not per display
Resistance, double-push, modifier and gate behaviours
Steps aside while you are dragging

features.title: Per-boundary rules
features.description: Each edge between two displays is configured on its own, because the boundary you keep crossing by accident is rarely the one you cross on purpose.

features.title: Deliberate crossings
features.description: Choose how much intent a crossing needs — slowing at the edge, a second push, a held modifier key, or a defined gate along the shared edge.

features.title: Desk profiles
features.description: Different setups get different behaviour, so docking and undocking does not mean reconfiguring.

privacyNote: Pointer behaviour is evaluated entirely on your Mac. Nothing about how you use your displays leaves the device.
